(1) Let p be a point in M n . The signature of g p is the signature of the quadratic
    form Q p (v) = g p (v, v) defined on T p M. This quadratic form is represented in
    local coordinates x : V ⊂ M → Rn by a matrix A(x) = (gi j (x)). The entries
    of this matrix are continuous functions of x, implying that its eigenvalues are
    also continuous functions of x. Indeed, they are the roots of the characteristic
    polynomial of A(x), whose coefficients are continuous functions of the entries
    of A(x). Since the eigenvalues of A(x) can never be zero (as g is nondegenerate,
    implying that A(x) is invertible) and M is connected, their signs cannot change
    and so the result follows.
